Senses.Explanation: The final phrase is a saying or verbal test claimed at the decisive end of an exchange or life. Yantou Quanhuo says Xuefeng does not understand it and answers a request to identify it with ‘just this’ (只者是), after distinguishing shared birth from shared death. Tianning Xipu, Foyan Qingyuan, Chaozong Tongren, Sixin Wuxin, and Yuanwu Keqin use it in praise, criticism, first-and-last-phrase testing, and warnings that a claimed understanding still does not pass. No universally fixed sentence is supplied.
Senses.Note: Six phrase/saying witnesses from six distinct works establish this verbal referent. The separately attested death-performance label is not merged into it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 頭云：「雪峰不會末後句。」僧請益巖頭。頭云：「雪峰與我同條生，不與我同條死。要識末後句，只者是。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Collected Summary of the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Guting (古庭禪師語錄輯略): Yantou Quanhuo utters both headword clauses in one continuous reply about Xuefeng Yicun.

Occurrences.Kwic: 偉哉大丈夫，不會末後句。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Huigong Xiong at Baoxiang Grove, South Sea (南海寶象林慧弓詗禪師語錄): Tianning Xipu utters the appraisal at the death scene.

Occurrences.Kwic: 忌晨上堂先師當年末後句與人皮下挑出
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Ancient Worthies (古尊宿語錄): Foyan Qingyuan utters the headword during a memorial-morning hall address.

Occurrences.Kwic: 要且未透末後句在。曹山則不然
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chaozong (朝宗禪師語錄): Chaozong Tongren utters the headword in his own comment after raising earlier masters.

Occurrences.Kwic: 死心問：會得最初句，便會末後句。會得末後句，便會最初句。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Orthodox Continuation of the Lamp (續燈正統), Longya Zhicai section: Sixin Wuxin is the exact quoted questioner uttering both headword clauses in one turn.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若恁麼會。也出雪竇末後句。不得在。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Blue Cliff Record by Chan Master Foguo Yuanwu (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄): Yuanwu Keqin utters the headword in his own commentary on Xuedou Chongxian’s verse.

Senses.PreferredTarget: the final act of dying seated or standing
Senses.Explanation: The same graphs also label a death-performance rather than a phrase. Zhongfeng Mingben explicitly reports that dying seated or standing is called the ‘final phrase’ (坐脫立亡喚作末後句). This one explicit witness establishes a different act-referent but does not make that later classification corpus-wide.
Senses.Note: One explicit work; kept provisional and distinct from the verbal final phrase.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Extensive Record of Tianmu Zhongfeng (天目中峰廣錄): Zhongfeng Mingben states the attested naming formula in his own prose.
